R001.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The h identity starts at hv=lambda v, and h y^(t+1)v=y h y^t v-2y^(t+1)v=(lambda-2(t+1))y^(t+1)v. For x the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=lambda v. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. Discharge each step hypothesis and apply natural induction. Thus F001 holds for all natural t, with the x formula used only for t>=1.

H003 gives lambda>=0, so |I|=lambda+1=n>0. Iterating F001, for i in I, x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v!=0: when i=0 the product is 1; otherwise all i factors of the descending product are positive integers and v!=0 by H006. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give all the asserted basis and operator formulas.

R002.text: By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. Their restrictions satisfy the same commutator identities. H001 makes R the subring obtained by inverting integers prime to p. H007 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V; N001 gives complex dimension n and |I|=n, so that basis has n elements and can be indexed by I.

Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. Each X_r,Y_r is complex-linear and preserves M by F001, so preserves this R-span.

Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)Q=E_(i,lambda), since the surviving coefficient is binom(lambda-i,lambda-i)=1. Finally Q Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j). Indeed an input e_k with k<j goes below e_lambda and is killed by Q; for k>j it goes past the lowering string and vanishes; and e_j maps with coefficient binom(lambda,lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j). These statements include lambda=0. By H001 and H003, lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! have no prime factor p. The factorial identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then shows p does not divide binom(lambda,j), so its rational inverse lies in R.

Composing the three identities in F003 and using the defining action of matrix units gives E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) for every i,j in I. All factors preserve iota(M_R) by F002, and the scalar is in R by F003, hence every E_ij preserves it. F001-F003 and this formula establish all the asserted localization and matrix-unit properties. No weights modulo p were separated.

R003.text: By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.

R004.text: By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. This scalar is defined and nonzero, because N002 states that binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and a unital homomorphism to a field maps units to units.

For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove all the asserted basis, scalar-extension and operator properties, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

R005.text: Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j2 in the formula for T_(i,j2) lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j2) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_(i,j2), hence under all matrix units since i,j2 were arbitrary.

Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. By H003, for p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1, and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.

194: Actual tier and per-response usage coverage remain unknown when not exposed. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
195: 
196: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
197: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated native Codex carrier requests
198: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
199: and record each stage's selected profile;
200: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

hypotheses.statement: The field K has characteristic p.

L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.
n=lambda+1.
I={i in Z: 0<=i<=lambda}.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. When 0 belongs to I this is J_0; the definition does not assume that the different J_i agree.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

definitions.type: K-linear Lie algebra representation of L_K on V_K
definitions.definition: rho is the action induced by the lattice operators: for t in {x,y,h}, rho(t tensor 1)(m tensor c)=(tm) tensor c, extended K-linearly to L_K. The action is defined when the lattice operators preserve M and satisfy the Chevalley relations.
x_K=rho(x tensor 1).
y_K=rho(y tensor 1).
h_K=rho(h tensor 1).

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: X_r^K, also denoted (X_K)_r, is induced by X_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (X_r m) tensor c.

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: Y_r^K, also denoted (Y_K)_r, is induced by Y_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (Y_r m) tensor c.
F_p=Z/pZ with its field structure for the prime p. For K of characteristic p its canonical embedding in K sends the residue class of an integer to that integer times 1_K.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary format-4 audit to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

201: Resolve the confirmed concurrency before dispatch and record its basis; do not
202: claim an unknown backend maximum. N limits local R-node reviews, then local
203: Lean proof jobs in a later phase. NL0 authoring, global Audit A, preparation,
204: interface work, assembly and Audit B use one serial lane per case.
205: Count root/controller, worker, review and retry calls. Cached/reasoning tokens
206: are subsets of input/output totals, not extra tokens. Missing usage is unknown.
207: 
208: Return the exact accepted scope, source/formal artifacts, unresolved citations
209: or gaps, actual execution health, time/token breakdown, and reproducible commands.
210: Do not claim a universal NL0 compiler, an unconditional proof of literature
211: inputs, completed Audit C, or acceleration from this prototype alone.

value.statement: n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.

1: # Local NL0 extraction and incremental-review record
2: 
3: Use [the procedure](../references/source-refactoring.md) and
4: [executable guide](../references/integrated-workflow.md). This worksheet is not
5: itself an acceptance record; the adapter validates the actual JSON reviews.
6: All review fields begin UNVERIFIED and can
7: change only after actual inspection. Keep the baseline files immutable.
8: 
9: ## Baseline and scope
10: 
11: - Baseline canonical graph/spec paths and SHA256:
12: - Baseline Audit A path/SHA256, exact scope, actual status and reviewer disclosure:
13: - Baseline evidence verified; outstanding FAIL/UNVERIFIED items:
14: - Revised package directory and revision identity:
15: - Operation: translation-preparation proof factoring, not NL0 reconstruction.
16: - Protected original target/H/D/E/M/logic/pins and existing N/P statements:
17: - Candidate IDs and proposed edit allowlist:
18: - Mathematical author, delta reviewer and actual prior exposure:
19: 
20: ## One record per candidate
21: 
22: - Candidate ID:
23: - Existing exported N usable instead of new extraction? Explain:
24: - Repeated occurrences: exact old R IDs and JSON pointers/paragraph spans:
25: - Avoided repeated work expected; basis and unmeasured assumptions:
26: - Proposed new N/R IDs:
27: - Full statement with all binders, domains and conditions:
28: - Direct inputs and their roles:
29: - Existing derivation to copy, its source spans and required local context:
30: - Any temporary assumption, witness, choice, definition guard or escaping local:
31: - Why this is an existing derivation, without stronger/generalized mathematics:
32: - Eligibility judgment and actual evidence: UNVERIFIED
33: - Candidate outcome: UNVERIFIED / STAGED / DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL / REJECTED
34: 
35: ## Patch manifest
36: 
37: | Stable ID / JSON pointer | Before hash / exact span | After hash / exact span | Permitted edit and reason |
38: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
39: 
40: - New producer proof and its mapping to old derivation spans:
41: - Every changed consumer input/citation/application record:
42: - All other mathematical records/spans preserved:
43: - Global graph/spec check command, actual output and artifact hashes:
44: - Cycle/reachability/definition-guard/producer checks:
45: - New source package hashes and actual diff artifact:
46: - Unexplained changes: UNVERIFIED
47: 
48: ## New producer review
49: 
50: Apply the ordinary Audit A obligations to the full new N/R. Record actual
51: source applications and the fresh packet-only replay separately.
52: 
53: - Complete statement, objects and dependency closure: UNVERIFIED
54: - Inputs, argument, accounting and exact output: UNVERIFIED
55: - Scope, guards and E/M applicability: UNVERIFIED
56: - Fresh replay carrier/input boundary, packet hash and evidence: UNVERIFIED
57: - Review verdict and located evidence: UNVERIFIED
58: - Scope: producer packet only; whole-graph acceptance and comparison to the old
59:   derivation belong to the separate substitution/evidence checks.
60: 
61: ## One substitution review per consumer
62: 
63: - Consumer R ID and exact replaced span:
64: - This consumer's old derivation and the separate supplier derivation for the
65:   shared producer; compare intermediate conclusions, not consumer final goals:
66: - Exact reviewed cut packet SHA256; inherited evidence and actual exposure:
67: - Old conclusion at the cut, with binders/conditions/conventions:
68: - Shared theorem instantiation and exact supplied conclusion:
69: - Evidence discharging every application condition:
70: - Facts/objects/values/scopes needed by the unchanged continuation:
71: - Evidence that these remain available and unchanged:
72: - Old source/application accounting and its exact replacement:
73: - Unchanged region hashes and precise baseline judgments inherited:
74: - New judgments covering the changed boundary, with located evidence:
75: - Exposure: delta review with baseline access, not a fresh whole-R replay.
76: - Boundary review verdict: UNVERIFIED
77: - Review the actual source format: N calls use direct inputs/prose, while
78:   `applications` records belong only to E/M; do not require invalid N records.
79: - The shared application replaces the selected derivation rather than merely
80:   adding an annotation; actual before/after evidence: UNVERIFIED
81: - If not local, defer the candidate instead of expanding to whole-case review:
82: 
83: ## Coverage and disposition
84: 
85: - Baseline + new reviews cover each revised proof region; coverage evidence:
86: - Inherited unresolved items and currently blocked descendants:
87: - Actual discovery/edit/check/review elapsed time and any model/tool faults:
88: - Record status: UNVERIFIED / DELTA-REVIEW-PASSED / DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL / REJECTED
89: - Accepted source revision, or baseline retained; exact reason:
90: - Executable acceptance: source_preparation.py check result and
91:   source-acceptance.json; baseline and all new evidence revalidated by Audit B.
92: - Actual inherited baseline qualifications and reviewer exposure:
93: - Pending work before production acceptance and worker-packet generation:
94: 
95: ## Boundary example
96: 
97: Suppose old R010 and R020 each explicitly derive L(x) from A and B, then use it
98: in different continuations. Copy one complete derivation into a new producer
99: of `for every x in the stated domain, A(x) and B(x) imply L(x)`. At each actual
100: occurrence, keep the same x, discharge A(x)/B(x), and replace only that proof
101: span by this application. Review the new closed statement and each cut.
102: 
103: Do not replace a span that also selected a witness w used later by a theorem
104: merely asserting `there exists w`: that may lose the required value/scope.
105: Defer the extraction unless the exact continuation interface can be preserved.
106: These examples explain the review method; they are not executed controls or
107: evidence that a model correctly follows it.

1: # Mathematically reviewed background in Yui
2: 
3: Audit A's shared section is the mathematical authority. The policy is
4: mathematical-background-v2-1. Ordinary mathematics is reviewed in NL0; exact
5: Mathlib implementation is resolved in nl02lean.
6: 
7: ## Eligibility and record
8: 
9: A note records a correct, routine local step with actual available premises,
10: no new hypothesis, no missing project lemma and no new core proof route.
11: Give id (BG001 etc.), kind (elementary or mathematical), at (an existing
12: /inference/argument/N/text pointer), fact (precise mathematical statement),
13: grounds ([{location,reason}] for real available conditions), and justification
14: (actual mathematical reasoning). A familiar name alone is insufficient.
15: Non-native notes have no source field or claim of a verified Lean declaration.
16: The optional record_background_note tool saves a checkpoint; a complete review
17: may submit all its notes in one artifact without separate tool calls.
18: 
19: For example, continuity of a sum follows from the supplied continuity of the
20: functions and continuous addition on their actual codomain. Check those
21: conditions mathematically. The reviewer need not call Lean or identify
22: Continuous.add before judging that routine step.
23: 
24: Substantive missing arguments, changed quantifiers, missing witness existence,
25: unsupported limit exchanges and uncertain external statements remain blocking.
26: The controller validates structure and local pointers; it never decides that
27: a mathematical fact is true or routine. An actual independent reviewer owns
28: that decision and may return FAIL or UNVERIFIED.
29: 
30: ## Handoff
31: 
32: The immutable author graph and hash-bound review notes jointly describe the
33: accepted mathematical proof. The format-4 receipt is not a format-3 verified native
34: background policy. Explicit native mathlib notes can still be inspected only
35: with their complete matching pinned evidence; they are optional, not a new
36: requirement for routine mathematical notes.
37: 
38: Normal translation uses node_local_reference. Notes travel with their own
39: paragraphs and do not become additional premise ports. Workers find appropriate
40: library declarations or prove auxiliary facts with their actual conditions.
41: The interface author chooses shared representations, not every local tactic
42: or implementation lemma in advance. Every required fact must eventually be
43: established in checked Lean. No note is an axiom or a new external E.
44: 
45: The source supplement hash and exact notes are bound in the interface contract,
46: worker packets and Audit B source inventory. They cannot be dropped, borrowed
47: from another node or relabeled as native evidence. Mathematical changes return
48: to affected Audit A scopes; representation-only changes remain reviewed Lean
49: work. Ordinary pinned Mathlib use needs no NL0 theorem-use ledger.
